questions.title: Hyperlinks
questions.prompt: Which HTML element creates a clickable link?
questions.hint: Think of the word 'anchor'.
questions.explanation: The a tag makes a link. Its href attribute sets where the link goes.

questions.title: String length
questions.prompt: What does this Python code print?
questions.hint: Count every letter, including capitals.
questions.explanation: len() counts characters. D-e-v-Q-u-e-s-t has 8.

questions.title: Stack order
questions.prompt: A stack follows which ordering rule?
questions.hint: Think of a stack of plates.
questions.explanation: A stack is LIFO: the last item added is the first one removed.

questions.title: Flutter language
questions.prompt: Which language are Flutter apps written in?
questions.hint: It starts with the letter D.
questions.explanation: Flutter apps are written in Dart. Swift and Kotlin are for native iOS and Android.

questions.title: Version control
questions.prompt: Which tool is the most widely used for version control?
questions.hint: It tracks changes to files over time.
questions.explanation: Git records every change to your code, so you can review, undo and combine work safely.

questions.title: SQL injection
questions.prompt: Which attack puts malicious SQL into user input?
questions.hint: It targets the database query itself.
questions.explanation: SQL injection tricks a database into running commands the developer never intended. Parameterised queries prevent it.

questions.title: HTTPS port
questions.prompt: What is the default port for HTTPS?
questions.hint: HTTP uses port 80.
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses port 443 by default and encrypts the traffic sent on it.

questions.title: Hidden files
questions.prompt: Which command lists all files, including hidden ones?
questions.hint: The -a flag means 'all'.
questions.explanation: ls -a shows files whose names start with a dot, such as .bashrc.

questions.title: Containers
questions.prompt: Which tool packages an app and its dependencies into a container?
questions.hint: Its logo is a whale.
questions.explanation: Docker bundles an app with everything it needs, so it runs the same way on any machine.

questions.title: Filtering rows
questions.prompt: Which SQL keyword keeps only the rows that match a condition?
questions.hint: It comes right after FROM.
questions.explanation: WHERE keeps only the rows that match your condition.

questions.title: Training data
questions.prompt: What does a machine learning model learn from during training?
questions.hint: Think about what teaches a student.
questions.explanation: Models learn patterns from example data. The quality of that data shapes the results.

questions.title: Average
questions.prompt: What is the mean of 2, 4 and 6?
questions.hint: Add them up, then divide by how many there are.
questions.explanation: The mean is the sum divided by the count: (2 + 4 + 6) ÷ 3 = 4.

questions.title: Light sensors
questions.prompt: Which component turns light into an electrical signal?
questions.hint: Think about what a camera does.
questions.explanation: A photodiode is a sensor that converts light into a signal a microcontroller can read.

questions.title: Tamper-proof records
questions.prompt: What makes a blockchain hard to change?
options: Each block stores a hash of the previous block
It is kept on one computer
questions.hint: Changing one block would break the link to the next.
questions.explanation: Each block stores a fingerprint of the one before it, so changing old records is easy to detect.

questions.title: Contrast
questions.prompt: Why does colour contrast matter in interface design?
options: It helps people read text clearly
It removes the need for fonts
questions.hint: Think about people with low vision.
questions.explanation: Good contrast makes text readable for more people, including those with low vision or in bright light.

questions.title: Logo file format
questions.prompt: Which format keeps a logo sharp at any size?
questions.hint: It is built from paths and shapes.
questions.explanation: SVG is a vector format, so it scales to any size. JPG and PNG are made of pixels.

questions.title: Frame rate
questions.prompt: What does FPS stand for in games?
questions.hint: It measures how smooth the picture looks.
questions.explanation: FPS counts how many images the screen shows each second. Higher usually means smoother motion.

questions.title: Current folder
questions.prompt: Which terminal command shows the folder you are in?
questions.hint: It stands for 'print working directory'.
questions.explanation: pwd prints the path of the folder you are currently in.

questions.title: Triggers
questions.prompt: In a no-code automation tool, what is a trigger?
options: The event that starts the workflow
questions.hint: It is what starts the workflow running.
questions.explanation: A trigger is the event, such as a new form submission, that starts an automated workflow.

questions.title: Strong CV
questions.prompt: What should a strong tech CV show first?
options: A long list of tools only
questions.hint: Employers want evidence of what you built.
questions.explanation: Recruiters look for what you have built and the impact it had, so put projects and results near the top.
